claims.text: Grusch, quoted in The Debrief on 5 June 2023: 'Individuals on these UAP programs approached me in my official capacity and disclosed their concerns regarding a multitude of wrongdoings, such as illegal contracting against the Federal Acquisition Regulations and other criminality and the suppression of information across a qualified industrial base and academia.'
Charles McCullough III filed a Disclosure of Urgent Concern(s) and Complaint of Reprisal on Grusch's behalf with the Intelligence Community Inspector General in May 2022.
The Intelligence Community Inspector General found the complaint 'credible and urgent' in July 2022.

Grusch testified under oath on 26 July 2023 before the House Oversight subcommittee at the hearing 'Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena: Implications on National Security, Public Safety, and Government Transparency', with Ryan Graves and David Fravor.

Grusch's written testimony states he was 'informed in the course of my official duties of a multi-decade UAP crash retrieval and reverse engineering program' to which he was denied access, and refers to 'Non-Human Reverse Engineering Programs'.

Grusch's written testimony to the House Oversight Committee contains no discussion of funding mechanisms, budget lines, or contractor financial arrangements; the financial specifics were reserved for classified session.

The named mechanism in the allegation is procurement rather than appropriation: 'illegal contracting against the Federal Acquisition Regulations' describes government money reaching a contractor under an instrument that does not comply with the rules determining what the government gets for it - which is the precise legal condition under which recovered material could sit in private custody while having been paid for with federal funds. Reasoning: the FAR governs data rights, property title and cost allowability; contracting outside it is how title would fail to pass.

desc: The specific allegation that programme funds were moved into private contractor custody outside congressional oversight has a named source, a date, a legal vehicle and an oath. David Charles Grusch, formerly the National Reconnaissance Office's representative to the Unidentified Aerial Phenomena Task Force and a senior technical adviser on UAP analysis at the National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency, filed a Disclosure of Urgent Concern and Complaint of Reprisal with the Intelligence Community Inspector General in May 2022, through counsel Charles McCullough III - himself a former Intelligence Community Inspector General. The ICIG found the complaint credible and urgent in July 2022. Grusch then briefed the staffs of the congressional intelligence committees in closed session. On 5 June 2023 he went on the record with Leslie Kean and Ralph Blumenthal in The Debrief, stating: 'Individuals on these UAP programs approached me in my official capacity and disclosed their concerns regarding a multitude of wrongdoings, such as illegal contracting against the Federal Acquisition Regulations and other criminality and the suppression of information across a qualified industrial base and academia.' That sentence is the named mechanism: not a generic accusation of secrecy but a specific claim of procurement fraud - contracting conducted outside the Federal Acquisition Regulation, which is the body of law governing how the government buys things and what the government owns when it has paid. On 26 July 2023 Grusch testified under oath before the Subcommittee on National Security, the Border, and Foreign Affairs of the House Committee on Oversight and Accountability, at a hearing titled 'Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena: Implications on National Security, Public Safety, and Government Transparency', alongside Ryan Graves and Commander David Fravor. His written statement records that he was 'informed in the course of my official duties of a multi-decade UAP crash retrieval and reverse engineering program' to which he was denied access, and refers to 'Non-Human Reverse Engineering Programs'; the specific financial detail he declined to give in open session, offering it in a classified setting. Five months later Congress enacted section 1687 of the FY2024 NDAA, barring funds for unreported UAP special access activity and barring UAP-related contractor independent research and development from being an allowable indirect cost. The sequence - complaint, credible-and-urgent finding, closed briefings, sworn testimony, statute naming IR&D - is the strongest documented chain on this board connecting an allegation about money to legislative action about money.

claims.source: Leslie Kean and Ralph Blumenthal, "Intelligence Officials Say U.S. Has Retrieved Craft of Non-Human Origin," The Debrief, June 5, 2023, https://thedebrief.org/intelligence-officials-say-u-s-has-retrieved-non-human-craft/
claims.text: In May 2022 Charles McCullough III, the first Senate-confirmed Inspector General of the Intelligence Community (2011, under DNI James Clapper), filed a "Disclosure of Urgent Concern(s); Complaint of Reprisal" with the ICIG on David Grusch's behalf.

The Intelligence Community Inspector General found Grusch's complaint "credible and urgent" in July 2022, and a summary was submitted to Director of National Intelligence Avril Haines, the Senate Select Committee on Intelligence, and the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence.

The unclassified version of the complaint states that Grusch has direct knowledge that UAP-related classified information has been withheld and/or concealed from Congress by "elements" of the intelligence community "to purposely and intentionally thwart legitimate Congressional oversight of the UAP Program."

All testimony Grusch provided for the classified complaint was given under oath, and the complaint closed with his signature attached to the statement "I do solemnly affirm under the penalties of perjury that the contents of the foregoing paper are true and correct to the best of my knowledge."

claims.source: House Oversight and Accountability Subcommittee on National Security, the Border, and Foreign Affairs hearing transcript, July 26, 2023, https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/CHRG-118hhrg53022/html/CHRG-118hhrg53022.htm
claims.text: Under oath on July 26, 2023 Grusch testified: "I was informed in the course of my official duties of a multi-decade UAP crash retrieval and reverse engineering program to which I was denied access to those additional read-ons when I requested it."
Asked by Rep. Jared Moskowitz how such a program is funded, Grusch testified: "I will give you generalities. I can get very specific in a closed session. But misappropriation of funds and self-fund."

Asked whether he had met people with direct knowledge of non-human origin craft, Grusch testified: "Yes. I personally interviewed those individuals." He did not testify to first-hand observation of craft or materials.

Asked when U.S. contact with non-human intelligence first occurred, Grusch testified: "I like to use the term nonhuman. I do not like to denote origin. Keeps the aperture open both scientifically. Certainly, like I have discussed publicly, previously 1930's."

In statements cleared for open publication by the DoD Office of Prepublication and Security Review on April 4 and 6, 2023, Grusch alleged "illegal contracting against the Federal Acquisition Regulations and other criminality and the suppression of information across a qualified industrial base and academia."

Grusch served as the National Reconnaissance Office representative to the UAP Task Force from 2019 to 2021 and as the National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency's co-lead for UAP analysis and task force representative from late 2021 to July 2022, as a GS-15 cleared at TS/SCI; he left government on April 7, 2023.

Grusch helped draft the UAP language in the FY2023 National Defense Authorization Act, spearheaded by Senators Kirsten Gillibrand and Marco Rubio and signed into law in December 2022 -- the provisions now codified at 50 U.S.C. 3373b.

Retired Army Colonel Karl E. Nell, the Army's liaison to the UAP Task Force from 2021 to 2022, stated on the record: "His assertion concerning the existence of a terrestrial arms race occurring sub-rosa over the past eighty years focused on reverse engineering technologies of unknown origin is fundamentally correct, as is the indisputable realization that at least some of these technologies of unknown origin derive from non-human intelligence."

claims.source: 50 U.S.C. 3373b(b), enacted as Pub. L. 117-263, div. A, title XVI, sec. 1673, Dec. 23, 2022, 136 Stat. 2959, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=(title:50+section:3373b)
claims.text: 50 U.S.C. 3373b(b)(1)(A) provides that an authorized disclosure "shall not be subject to a nondisclosure agreement entered into by the individual who makes the disclosure," and 3373b(b)(2)(A) prohibits reprisal including revocation or suspension of security clearances.

claims.source: ODNI memorandum ES 2026-00818, "Preliminary Guidance for Implementation of NDA Waivers," July 31, 2026, reproduced in full at https://douglasmmessier.substack.com/p/guidance-published-for-uap-disclosure
claims.text: On July 31, 2026, Principal Deputy Director of National Intelligence Aaron Lukas issued memorandum ES 2026-00818 directing that prior nondisclosure agreements, oaths and commitments are waived for current and former government employees and contractors speaking to AARO or to authorized representatives of the Presidential Unsealing and Reporting System for UAP Encounters (PURSUE) Task Force.

connections: Charles McCullough III designed and ran the ICIG whistleblower channel he later used on Grusch's behalf -- the complainant's counsel is the architect of the mechanism.
Karl E. Nell corroborated Grusch on the record and appears again in manhattan-project-2 as the proponent of a state-scale reverse-engineering effort.

Christopher Mellon, former Deputy Assistant Secretary of Defense for Intelligence, said he had received detailed information from well-placed officials about the alleged program including 'the history, governing documents and the location where a craft was allegedly abandoned and recovered.'

Jonathan Grey of the National Air and Space Intelligence Center at Wright-Patterson AFB went on the record in the same June 5, 2023 report asserting the existence of 'complex historical programs involving the coordinated retrieval and study of exotic materials, dating back to the early 20th century.'
The funding mechanism Grusch alleges is the one described in classified-annex; the program-structure mechanism is the one described in dodi-5205-11.
AARO's KONA BLUE disclosure is the Department's competing origin story for the same allegation set, tracing it to AAWSAP/AATIP, DIA and Bigelow Aerospace rather than to a legacy program.

Senators Kirsten Gillibrand and Marco Rubio sponsored the FY2023 NDAA UAP provisions Grusch helped draft; Reps. Tim Burchett, Anna Paulina Luna, Jared Moskowitz, Nancy Mace and Eric Burlison questioned him at the July 26, 2023 hearing.
dossier.denialPosture: Pentagon spokesperson Sue Gough stated that the Department had not discovered "any verifiable information to substantiate claims that any programs regarding the possession or reverse-engineering of extraterrestrial materials have existed in the past or exist currently," and separately that it had "no information that any individual has been harmed or killed as a result of providing information." AARO's 2024 historical review states it "found no empirical evidence" for reverse-engineering claims and attributes them to "circular reporting from a group of individuals who believe this to be the case." Both are dated, attributable statements from institutions Grusch named as concealing; neither addresses the misappropriation-of-funds charge on its own terms.
dossier.narrative:
Precision matters more here than anywhere else on the board, because the allegation has been repeatedly restated in forms Grusch never used.

What he filed: in May 2022, Charles McCullough III -- senior partner at Compass Rose Legal Group, and the original Inspector General of the Intelligence Community, confirmed by the Senate in 2011 under DNI James Clapper -- filed on Grusch's behalf a "Disclosure of Urgent Concern(s); Complaint of Reprisal" with the ICIG. The complaint concerned information Grusch had gathered beginning in 2019 while working with the UAP Task Force. All testimony Grusch provided for the classified complaint was given under oath, and the document closed with his signed affirmation: "I do solemnly affirm under the penalties of perjury that the contents of the foregoing paper are true and correct to the best of my knowledge."

What the unclassified version of the complaint says: that Grusch has direct knowledge that UAP-related classified information has been withheld and concealed from Congress by "elements" of the intelligence community "to purposely and intentionally thwart legitimate Congressional oversight of the UAP Program." Note the construction -- withheld from Congress, intentionally, to defeat oversight. That is an allegation about a crime against the legislature, not about biology.

What the ICIG did: found the complaint "credible and urgent" in July 2022. This is a procedural determination under the urgent-concern statute -- it means the complaint met the threshold for transmission, not that its substance was adjudicated true. Per Grusch, a summary went immediately to DNI Avril Haines, the Senate Select Committee on Intelligence, and the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence. A whistleblower reprisal investigation was opened. Several current members of the alleged recovery program spoke to the Inspector General's office and, per reporting, corroborated information Grusch had provided.

What he said under oath on July 26, 2023, before the House Oversight Subcommittee on National Security, the Border, and Foreign Affairs. The core sentence: "I was informed in the course of my official duties of a multi-decade UAP crash retrieval and reverse engineering program to which I was denied access to those additional read-ons when I requested it." Two things are asserted and one is not. Asserted: that he was officially informed such a program exists, and that he formally requested and was denied read-on. Not asserted: that he saw craft, materials or bodies himself. Every subsequent claim of first-hand observation attributed to him is a media artifact.

On funding, Representative Jared Moskowitz asked directly. Grusch: "I will give you generalities. I can get very specific in a closed session. But misappropriation of funds and self-fund." Two mechanisms, not one. Misappropriation -- money appropriated for a stated purpose spent on another. Self-fund -- the effort generating its own revenue, presumably through the commercial exploitation of derived technology, which would place private contractors inside the financial architecture rather than merely adjacent to it.

On sourcing, asked whether he had met people with direct knowledge of non-human origin craft, he answered: "Yes. I personally interviewed those individuals." On timeline, asked when contact first occurred: "I like to use the term nonhuman. I do not like to denote origin. Keeps the aperture open both scientifically. Certainly, like I have discussed publicly, previously 1930's." On the campaign against public knowledge, in response to Representative Anna Paulina Luna, he referred to "a multi-decade, you know, campaign to disenfranchise public interest."

His pre-hearing DOPSR-cleared statements go further on the contracting angle: "Individuals on these UAP programs approached me in my official capacity and disclosed their concerns regarding a multitude of wrongdoings, such as illegal contracting against the Federal Acquisition Regulations and other criminality and the suppression of information across a qualified industrial base and academia." He also characterized the effort as a "publicly unknown Cold War for recovered and exploited physical material -- a competition with near-peer adversaries over the years to identify UAP crashes/landings and retrieve the material for exploitation/reverse engineering to garner asymmetric national defense advantages."

The corroboration that matters is Karl E. Nell's, because Nell put his name to it while identifying himself by his official role. Nell, the Army's liaison to the UAP Task Force from 2021 to 2022, said: "His assertion concerning the existence of a terrestrial arms race occurring sub-rosa over the past eighty years focused on reverse engineering technologies of unknown origin is fundamentally correct, as is the indisputable realization that at least some of these technologies of unknown origin derive from non-human intelligence." Nell also called Grusch "beyond reproach."

The institutional counter-position arrived in 2024. AARO's historical review concluded: "AARO found no empirical evidence for claims that the USG and private companies have been reverse-engineering extraterrestrial technology," and attributed the narrative "in large part" to "circular reporting from a group of individuals who believe this to be the case." AARO further asserts that "all the authentic programs have been properly notified and reported to Congress through the congressional defense and/or intelligence committees." That last sentence is a testable claim, and it is testable only against the classified annex.

As of 2026 the legal obstacle Grusch cited has formally been removed. On July 31, 2026, Principal Deputy Director of National Intelligence Aaron Lukas issued memorandum ES 2026-00818 directing that prior nondisclosure agreements, oaths and commitments are waived for current and former employees and contractors speaking to AARO or to the PURSUE Task Force. The corroboration Grusch said existed in closed session is now, on paper, free to speak.
openQuestions: Which appropriations accounts Grusch alleges were raided, and in what amounts -- he said he could 'get very specific in a closed session' and no unclassified specificity has followed.
What 'self-fund' means operationally: whether it denotes commercial revenue from derived technology, contractor cost-recovery, or something else.
Whether the ICIG reprisal investigation opened after July 2022 was ever completed, and what it found.
The identities of the more than forty individuals Grusch says he interviewed, and whether any have testified in closed session.
Whether the corroborating current members of the alleged program who spoke to the ICIG's office have been re-interviewed under the 2026 NDA waiver regime.
Whether AARO's assertion that 'all the authentic programs have been properly notified and reported to Congress' has ever been independently verified against the classified schedules.
dossier.whatItIs: A protected whistleblower complaint and subsequent sworn congressional testimony by David Charles Grusch, a former Air Force officer, National Reconnaissance Office senior intelligence officer and National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency co-lead for UAP analysis, alleging that a multi-decade U.S. crash-retrieval and reverse-engineering program exists, is concealed from Congress, and is sustained by the misappropriation of appropriated funds. The complaint was filed with the Intelligence Community Inspector General in May 2022 by Charles McCullough III, the first Senate-confirmed ICIG.
dossier.whyImplicated: This is the only allegation of its kind that has passed through a statutory inspector-general channel, been assessed as credible and urgent, been transmitted to the Director of National Intelligence and both intelligence committees, and then been repeated under oath in open session with the penalty of perjury attached. The specific charge is not that craft exist; it is a financial-crimes charge -- that money appropriated by Congress for other purposes was diverted, and that the diversion was the concealment method. That reframes the question from metaphysics to auditability. Grusch's counsel is the man who built the ICIG whistleblower system, which means the filing was engineered to survive procedurally. And Grusch's own hand appears in the FY2023 NDAA UAP language, so the statutory tripwires now on the books were drafted by the complainant against the mechanism he was complaining about.
